content: Okay so here's my calculator! I think it'd be cool to, slowly over time maybe, create a full list of all the effects that increase dmg and where they are in the calculation so that the calculator can be ehh... overly specific for no reason

<@1473096234276229172> So here's what I understand of the formula. There are also annotations for this info and more inside the calc file. Let me know if any of this conflicts with any of your research.

I'll have you know that Additive increases vs Multiplicative increases are my pet peeve, so I pay close attention to this sort of stuff. There *are* examples of both "Base DMG %" and "Final DMG %" where some are mult. and some are add., but it's relatively easy to tell them apart;

The multiplicatives are typically written unconditionally, i.e. "Wielder's Base DMG +25%," and the additives are typically written conditionally, i.e. "This card's Final DMG +20%."

Notable is that the additives, once summed together, *become* a commutatively multiplicative element along with the others. DMG Amplification is also commutative within Base DMG, **but scaling __is not,__** so this description is incorrect.

I separate the formula itself into 5 steps:
- **1. ATK Base**
  - First, multiply the Attribute (ATK) by all Attribute bonuses, then __round up.__
  - Then, multiply by Scaling, then __round up.__
- **2. Base DMG**
  - __Round__ DMG Amplification up.
  - Sum all Additive Base% together. *(B.Bonus%)*
  - Multiply all Multiplicative Base% together. *(B.DMG%)* **¹**
  - Multiply (Step 1) × (DMG. Amp) × (B.DMG%) × (B.Bonus%)
- **3. Benefits**
  - Multiply each flat-value status by how much your DMG is benefitting from them; e.g. STR, typically at 100%, but occasionally other things, like 5× STR, or 200% of Shield, or 60% of Tentacle DMG, or even "50 per Strike played" *(5000% of Strike Commands)*
  - Sum together the results of each benefit.
  - Sum (Step 2) + (Benefits)
- **4. Final DMG**
  - Sum all Additive Final% together. *(F.Bonus%)*
  - Multiply all Multiplicative Final% together. *(F.DMG%)* **¹**
  - Multiply (Step 3) × (Weakness?) × (F.DMG%) × (F.Bonus%)
  - __Round up.__ **This is where the game displays the DMG, like on a card.**
- **5. Filters**
  - __Round__ Base Crit. DMG up, and halve this value if Blind. **²**
  - Sum that with any conditional or temporary Crit. DMG buffs. *(then add 100%.)*
  - Multiply all Vulnerabilities together (Vuln, Psychic Trauma, etc.) **¹**
  - Multiply all Resistances together (Fortress, etc.) **¹**
  - Multiply (Step 4) × (Crit. DMG) × (Vulnerabilities) × (Resistances)
  - __Round up.__ **This amount of DMG is dealt to the enemy.**

**¹** *These steps are for ease of reading. Technically, the things multiplied together here are commutative with everything else.*
**²** *I'm unsure exactly where the ceilings are in the Crit rounding. It could round before Blind, after Blind, or both (likely both).*

"    ATK Base

    First, multiply the Attribute (ATK) by all Attribute bonuses, then round up.
    Then, multiply by Scaling, then round up."

Almost correct. There's an annoying rounding interaction though, so in actuality it's:
       First, multiply the Attribute (ATK) by all Attribute bonuses, then round up.
       Then, multiply by AtkScaling%, then multiply by [ability-sourced base dmg+1], and *then* round up this product. I don't know why they implemented it like this, just that they did. 

Everything else looks like it's the same as my findings, just with less details on which sub-layers/categories exist.

I listed all the individual categories/sub-layers that are multiplicative with each other to make it easier to identify which bonuses belong in which category, that is to say which are additive. So for example where you say "Multiply all Multiplicative Base% together. (B.DMG%)" I list all the different categories of multipliers instead of leaving it vague. As always items within a category are additive.
As is obviously the case in math the order in which you multiply/divide a bunch of numbers doesn't matter, I agree with you there. 

You can easily test for yourself ingame that the formula I gave works, or use the spreadsheet https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VDTfBBYgMNyQwMb8Y_wywbZyUNjlmlzHbimIZaYLhmA/copy  
(Sorry in advance for the terrible colour scheme and bad structure, I'm aesthetically regarded. Also it's probably missing a few categories, it's a work in progress that I've mostly abandoned).
To make it easier to test I added a crude table with some of the more common modifiers, including most of the wheels, and dropdown menus to pick and choose which ones you're using.

Again, I made this sheet specifically to test which categories / sub-layers of damage modifiers exist and how they interact.
